blocks.value: **The `Pattern` class in `java.util.regex` stores the format of a regular expression.**

import java.util.regex.Pattern;
import java.util.regex.Matcher;
Pattern p = Pattern.compile("[A-F]{5,}.*");

**The `compile` method compiles the given regular expression into a pattern. A compiled pattern can speed up your program when the pattern is used frequently**: the parsing work happens once instead of on every call.
**The `Matcher` class stores a possible match between a pattern and a string:**
Matcher match = patternName.matcher(stringName);
The `matcher` method returns a `Matcher` object. Use `matches()` to check whether the regular expression given in the `Pattern` matches a string:
`"AAAAA"` is five characters from `A-F`, satisfying `{5,}`, and `.*` absorbs `"hhh"`.
find()
**`Matcher`'s `find()` method scans the input sequence looking for the next subsequence that matches the pattern.** It returns `true` if the pattern exists as a **substring**.
**`matches()` versus `find()`: the distinction that matters most:**
Use **`matches()`** to validate a whole value (is this a valid phone number?). Use **`find()`** to search inside text (does this password contain a digit?).
`find()` can also be called repeatedly to walk through every match:
`group()` returns the text that was actually matched.
Capturing groups
